findings.where: Nav bar (the binding strip), the logo at its left, at both widths
findings.fault: The logo is recoloured. Its arches and the MMM INFRA wordmark are pale yellow on the maroon binding, not the logo blue #0070C0 and grey #404040. Neither logo colour appears anywhere in the palette, so the client's mark becomes a tinted device of this direction.
findings.who_objects: Mark, who keeps the logo as his identity (value 7). The brief says the mark is never redrawn, and the house rule says a logo is never recoloured: where a ground does not suit it, the version or the ground changes, and a new version needs the client's yes.

findings.where: First screen, the 'write to me' margin note (the only call to action). Desktop: it sits alone in the left margin at mid-height. Phone: it sits under the tagline.
findings.fault: The page's one action carries the least weight on the first screen: small red handwriting at the far left edge, near nothing it belongs to, below the headline, tagline, aqueduct drawing and photo in the squint. Its text gives no email address, so a visitor whose device has no mail client, or who wants to copy the address, gets nothing.
findings.who_objects: Development-bank staff deciding whether to contact Mark. They scan the content column, not the margin, and many work in webmail. The first-visit trust rule asks for the email address in full as the link text.

findings.where: End of the page at both widths (there is no footer)
findings.fault: The page ends on the motion-sketch box, with no footer. The palette assigns the binding colour to 'nav, footer', but the footer never appears, so the tile never shows the contact address in a footer or where the line ends.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who reads to the bottom and looks there for the address. First-visit trust item 7 puts a contact route on every page. The layout round also needs the footer drawn in this look before it can place one.

findings.where: Hero headline 'Mark M. Moseley, infrastructure advisor', the 'Libre Caslon Text' type specimen and the article heading, at both widths
findings.fault: The ruled feints run through the middle of the large display letters rather than under them, so every headline looks struck through and its letters are harder to read.
findings.who_objects: A first-time reader taking in Mark's name and line. The ruling is meant to be paper the type sits on, not lines crossing it.

findings.where: Article specimen: the heading 'The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law' (desktop) and the script pull quote (both widths, worst on phone)
findings.fault: Snapping to the 32 px feint double-spaces both. The two-line heading has a full blank line between its halves on desktop, so it reads as two separate headings. On phone the pull quote breaks into four lines with wide gaps and becomes the largest, loosest block in the article.
findings.who_objects: An article reader, who has to put the heading back together and loses the quote's sentence across the gaps. The article page is the Read surface this tile must prove.

findings.where: Article specimen, the pull quote set in Nanum Pen Script
findings.fault: The handwriting face sets a two-to-four-line quote inside an article, beside the margin note. The tile's own type rule says Mark's hand is 'one note per view, the call to action in the margin, never body text'. Spent on an article quote as well, the hand no longer singles out the action.
findings.who_objects: Angélique and the layout round, who get two contradictory instructions for when to use the hand. A reader sees the handwriting as styling rather than as Mark's one note.

findings.where: Article specimen, the 'Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the ‘Abundance’ Challenge · Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF' row
findings.fault: This is the article's only link, but it looks like bold body text: dark ink, no underline, nothing that says it opens. 'Replay the note' on the same page is underlined, so two links get two treatments. The row's bottom rule sits on the last line of text, so it reads as an underline under only the last words. The row has no label saying why a 2026 lecture hangs off a 2024 post.
findings.who_objects: A reader looking for the paper or PDF, who may not realise the title can be clicked. Angélique, who has to copy this row each time she attaches a PDF.

findings.where: Hero, the aqueduct drawing below the tagline (desktop centre, phone below the photo)
findings.fault: The drawing is a clean vector diagram: compass-true arcs, one even line weight and machine hatching, with ends that stop dead rather than trail off. It reads as placed artwork, not ballpoint sketched onto the pad, which is what the direction carries over from its seed.
findings.who_objects: Mark and the founder, judging whether the legal pad feels like his own working paper. The direction card calls for the aqueduct 'sketched straight onto the pad in ballpoint, unframed, its ends trailing off'.

findings.where: The double margin line down the left of the pad, every screen
findings.fault: The margin rule comes out a thin dark olive-brown, not the legal pad's red. The palette lists 'Margin red … margin', but on the page only the note is red, so one of the pad's most recognisable marks is lost.
findings.who_objects: Mark, who picked the legal pad for its lawyerly associations. Without the red margin it reads more as generic lined paper.

findings.fault: A button is styled as an underlined prose link, the treatment the house reserves for links that go somewhere, so it is not clear whether it navigates or acts here.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who expects an underlined phrase to take them to another page. The house rule reserves the underline for navigation.

findings.where: Hero, the italic line 'Over 40 years of international infrastructure experience.'
findings.fault: The first screen states Mark's standing as a size claim of years. Nothing on the screen points to work that shows it: no named body or role beyond the tagline's one World Bank post.
findings.who_objects: Procurement-minded bank staff, who judge experience by project kind and region, not by a count of years. The brief asks for confidence without boasts (value 6).
